text:
maria: Quick question — who owns precedence between feature flags and rollout policies? We just had a canary in console set to 20% but a runtime flag forced a 0% route for some customers and it scrambled our A/B metrics.
raj: Hmm, which runtime flag? the one deployed in routing-service or the per-instance experiment flag? :thinking_face:
maria: routing-service. Example: console rollout (rollout-controller) had:\n```\nrollout: {id: r-2026-exp, split: [{variant: control, pct: 80}, {variant: new-model, pct: 20}], source: console}\nflag: {key: disable-new-model, value: true, source: runtime}\n```\nWhen header included `x-feature-disable-new-model: true` the router sent 100% to control even though console said 20%.
leo: That's been a long-standing ambiguity. We historically treat runtime "kill" flags as higher priority to allow ops to quickly stop traffic. But product expects console rollouts to be authoritative for experiments A/B. So two different mental models colliding.
sophie: This exactly caused telemetry drift — experiment samples dropped mid-run and we lost the signal. From product/metrics POV console == experiment source, runtime flags are for emergencies only. We need clearer rules.
anna: Proposal: define a precedence matrix and enforce via the routing API. Idea: emergency/runtime kills (explicit emergency=true) > console rollouts (experiments) > defaults. Also attach metadata to decision: `origin_of_truth` and `override_reason` so console and observability can show why a particular user saw variant X.
raj: I like that. Minimal API change: change /resolve route to return an extra header or JSON field: `effective_source: [console|runtime|default]` and `override_tag: [emergency|manual|none]`.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: routing-service v3.14.2 -> svc/routing (canary 10%) :rocket:
maria: Can we also add a soft guard: if a console rollout is marked `experiment:true` then runtime flags can only override if `emergency=true` and an entry is added to the audit log (pager or ticket). Otherwise runtime flagging should be refused or require a force override with justification.
leo: I'll open a PR to: 1) add `effective_source` and `override_tag` to /resolve, 2) add telemetry tag `override_source` for traces/metrics, 3) enforce guard where `runtime override` must set `emergency=true` to trump experiment rollouts. Will include migration notes for existing flags.
raj: Console UX change: show a small badge on rollout rows "Overridden by: runtime (emergency)" with link to audit. Also surface a timeline for changes so experiments can be trusted.
sophie: And we should add a regression alert: if effective_sample_rate for an experiment changes >5% without a console change, fire an alert to the experiment owner.
maria: Perfect. Action items: leo PR by EOW, product (sophie) to define exact alert thresholds and wording, ops to add audit requirement. If anyone has objections speak now.
leo: no objections, starting the branch now. :+1:
raj: I'll sketch the console badge mock and add to the design board.
maria: Thanks all — this should prevent future metric skews. :raised_hands:
